---
title: "Pinning"
---

*Pinning* is recording the exact state of every object in a commit so it can be
read back later -- and, for systems that support it, protecting that state with
a native reference that survives retention and cleanup. This walkthrough builds
a small dataset, pins it twice, reproduces reads from the first commit, and
shows how drift, verification, and garbage collection behave.

The dataset: an Icechunk repository of imaging data on S3, a Neon Postgres
database of metrics, and a directory of raw plate images.

## Register the objects

```bash
tether init
tether add zarr/imaging --kind icechunk s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk --branch main
tether add db/metrics   --kind neon --project-id prj-9f2 --database metrics --role runner
tether add raw/plate1   --kind file /mnt/instruments/plate1/
```

`add` writes manifests only; the systems are first contacted by `status`.
`--branch main` (the default) names the object's *upstream*: the first commit
pins its head, and later `tether pull` moves the object to wherever it is
then. `--at SNAPSHOT` starts from a chosen state instead (see
[Positions](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#positions-what-the-next-commit-records)):

```bash
tether status
```

```
dataset 0f2e9c7a11b3
       new  db/metrics  [neon/forkable]
       new  raw/plate1  [file/observed] unrecoverable
       new  zarr/imaging  [icechunk/forkable]
```

The tiers already tell you what pinning will mean for each object: Icechunk and
Neon are *Forkable* (a native ref will be created), the directory is *Observed*
(its state can be recorded but not re-read, hence `unrecoverable`).

## Pin: the first commit

```bash
tether commit -m "Baseline: plate1 imaging + metrics"
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6
  pinned db/metrics -> tether.0a1b2c3d.a91f0e2b77c3e5f6
  recorded raw/plate1 (not recoverable)
committed 8d5719841a09
```

What happened, per object:

| Object | State recorded | Pin created |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zarr/imaging` | `snapshot_id` of `main` | Icechunk tag `tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6` (immutable, excluded from expiry) |
| `db/metrics` | `lsn`, `next_xid` of `main` | protected Neon child branch `tether.0a1b2c3d.a91f0e2b77c3e5f6` at that LSN |
| `raw/plate1` | `count`, `size`, `digest` | none; the per-file listing is stored under `.tether/listings/` |

Then the manifests (and the listing) were committed to your jj/git repository as
`8d5719841a09`. Look at what was committed:

```bash
jj diff -r 8d571984      # or: git show --stat 8d571984
```

```
Added regular file .tether/objects/zarr/imaging.toml:
        1: key = "zarr/imaging"
        2: kind = "icechunk"
        3: recoverable = true
        ...
       15: [state]
       16: snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"
       18: [pin]
       19: id = "6674305d5e1f"
       20: ref = "tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6"
```

Pin ids are content-addressed from `(kind, locator identity, state)`. Commit
again without changing anything and every object is reported `unchanged`; no
new refs are created.

## Pin again after the data moves

Some time later the imaging repository gets a new commit on `main` and the
metrics database has been written to. Nobody in this checkout forked a
working branch, so the objects still sit at their pins; a fan-out shows
upstream has moved past them:

```bash
tether status --snapshot       # fingerprint now; plain `status` shows the last snapshot
```

```
dataset 0f2e9c7a11b3
    behind  db/metrics  [neon/forkable]
     clean  raw/plate1  [file/observed] unrecoverable
    behind  zarr/imaging  [icechunk/forkable]
```

`commit` alone would change nothing -- an object you did not touch keeps its
pin, as an untouched file keeps its contents. `pull` takes upstream, then
commit pins it (`commit --pull` does both):

```bash
tether pull
tether commit -m "Re-segmented plate1; metrics through 2026-09-04"
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.deb4861eb388e5f6
  pinned db/metrics -> tether.0a1b2c3d.0c31e7aa5f92e5f6
committed cfc66fa79c0a
```

Two commits now describe two complete, consistent-as-captured states of the
whole dataset. Compare them:

```bash
tether diff 8d571984 cfc66fa7 --content
```

```
    changed  db/metrics  [+0 -0 ~0 tables]
    changed  zarr/imaging  [+0 -0 ~3 nodes]
               modified  /labels  12 chunks
               modified  /masks  12 chunks
               modified  /  group metadata
```

(Neon has no native diff, so `db/metrics` shows only that it changed; Icechunk
reports the arrays whose chunks were rewritten.)

## Reproduce reads from a pinned commit

This is the payoff. Any process can resolve every object *as it was* at a
commit. From the CLI:

```bash
tether open zarr/imaging -r 8d571984
```

```
s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk#tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6
```

```bash
tether open db/metrics -r 8d571984
```

```
postgresql://runner@ep-quiet-lake-a1b2c3.us-west-2.aws.neon.tech/metrics?...
```

From Python, the same handles come with native objects attached:

```python
from tether import Repo
from tether.handles import IcechunkHandle, NeonHandle

repo = Repo.find(".")

imaging = repo.open("zarr/imaging", rev="8d571984")
assert isinstance(imaging, IcechunkHandle) and imaging.read_only
store = imaging.session.store          # read-only icechunk session at the tag
# zarr.open_group(store, mode="r") ...

metrics = repo.open("db/metrics", rev="8d571984")
assert isinstance(metrics, NeonHandle)
metrics.url                            # connection URL for the pinned branch
```

For reproducible jobs, set `TETHER_REV` instead of passing `rev` everywhere;
`repo.open(key)` then defaults to a read-only handle at that commit:

```bash
TETHER_REV=8d571984 python run_analysis.py
```

```python
repo = Repo.find(".")
handle = repo.open("zarr/imaging")    # read-only, pinned; no code change needed
```

Record `TETHER_REV` (or `repo.vcs.current_rev()`) and each object's `pin.id`
next to your results and any output can be traced back to the exact state of
every input:

```python
provenance = {
    "tether_rev": os.environ.get("TETHER_REV") or repo.vcs.current_rev(),
    "pins": {k: (m.pin.id if m.pin else None) for k, m in repo.objects.items()},
}
```

`raw/plate1` cannot be opened at a revision: it is Observed, and its state at
`8d571984` is a digest, not an address. Promote directories that must be
recoverable to an object store with versioning enabled and register single
objects with `--file versioned`, or put them in lakeFS.

## Drift

`status --snapshot` fingerprints everything, so drift surfaces the next time
you ask. The directory was registered with the default `--file immutable`, so
if a file under `/mnt/instruments/plate1/` changes (its *content* -- a `touch`
is not a change):

```bash
tether status --snapshot
```

```
error: [raw/plate1] immutable object 'raw/plate1' changed since it was committed;
re-register with acceptance to record the new state
```

That is deliberate: an "immutable" input silently changing is the worst kind of
drift. Either the change is legitimate (`tether remove raw/plate1` and `add` it
again, then commit) or something wrote where it should not have. Other objects
drift benignly: a system that moved past the pin shows `behind` and waits for
`pull`; a working branch that moved shows `modified` and is pinned by the next
commit.

## Verify

Pins are references *inside other systems*, and those systems have their own
operators. `verify` confirms they still resolve to what the manifests say:

```bash
tether verify                      # working-tree manifests, cheap checks
tether verify -r 8d571984 --deep   # actually open each pinned state
tether verify --all-history --deep # every commit in the repository
```

```
        ok  8d5719841a09:db/metrics
        ok  8d5719841a09:zarr/imaging
        ok  cfc66fa79c0a:db/metrics
        ok  cfc66fa79c0a:zarr/imaging
```

A report is `ok`, `drifted` (the ref exists but points elsewhere), `missing`
(the ref or snapshot is gone -- expired, deleted), or `unknown` (cannot tell
without `--deep`). `--all-history` streams every manifest at every commit
through one object reader and verifies each distinct pin once, so it stays fast
on long histories. Exit status is non-zero if anything is not `ok`, which makes
it a natural CI check.

## Garbage collection

Pins are created before the VCS commit lands, so an aborted commit -- or history
you rewrote or abandoned -- can leave native refs nothing references. `gc`
collects every pin id mentioned by any manifest in history or the working tree,
lists what exists natively, and releases the rest:

```bash
tether gc                 # dry run: print the plan
tether gc --no-dry-run    # release orphaned pins, prune unreferenced listings
```

```
plan: gc (1 write(s))
               unpin  zarr/imaging  [icechunk] tether.0a1b2c3d.3c80e6bda56de5f6  no manifest in history references it
```

Run `verify --all-history` first; `gc` trusts history, and a pin that is
referenced but broken is a `verify` finding, not a `gc` one. Deliberately
dropping history to release its pins, and cleaning up working branches, is
covered in [Reclaiming storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd).

## Recap

- `commit` pins every Pinnable/Forkable object and records the rest; the VCS
  commit id names the whole state.
- `open -r <rev>` / `TETHER_REV` resolve any object read-only at that commit.
- Observed objects record state but cannot be re-read; use versioned storage
  or lakeFS if you need to.
- `status --snapshot` catches drift; `verify` confirms pins still hold;
  `gc` releases pins no commit references.
